commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.

target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the

module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result

measured.

phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts (#24968)

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in the `iree.encoding.materialized_layout_target`
module attribute. Typed accessors live in
`DispatchCreation/MaterializedLayoutTarget.h`; `Encoding/Utils` cannot
depend on HAL because HAL/IR depends on Stream/IR, which depends on
`Encoding/Utils`. The header lists every behavior the attribute changes.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-assign-data-tiling-encodings` skips such
modules. It is a module pass so that no function pass has to read the
attribute. Its options carry the operation families and encoding
strategy, so printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep them. The
default operation families now come from one helper,
`getDefaultDataTilingOpTypes`.
- `iree-dispatch-creation-verify-materialized-layout-target` runs first
in the dispatch-creation pipeline, independent of the data-tiling
options. It rejects modules compiled for a different target, for several
targets or for none.

Resuming with `--compile-from` reuses the serialized device targets, so
a normal `iree-compile` flow does not retarget. The check guards
hand-edited IR and tools that rewrite device targets. Nothing sets the
attribute until #24969.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts (#24968)

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in the `iree.encoding.materialized_layout_target`
module attribute. Typed accessors live in
`DispatchCreation/MaterializedLayoutTarget.h`; `Encoding/Utils` cannot
depend on HAL because HAL/IR depends on Stream/IR, which depends on
`Encoding/Utils`. The header lists every behavior the attribute changes.

- `iree-dispatch-creation-assign-data-tiling-encodings` skips such
modules. It is a module pass so that no function pass has to read the
attribute. Its options carry the operation families and encoding
strategy, so printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep them. The
default operation families now come from one helper,
`getDefaultDataTilingOpTypes`.
- `iree-dispatch-creation-verify-materialized-layout-target` runs first
in the dispatch-creation pipeline, independent of the data-tiling
options. It rejects modules compiled for a different target, for several
targets or for none.

Resuming with `--compile-from` reuses the serialized device targets, so
a normal `iree-compile` flow does not retarget. The check guards
hand-edited IR and tools that rewrite device targets. Nothing sets the
attribute until #24969.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[SPIRV] Fix WebGPU SPIR-V client API detection (#25051)

`deduceClientAPI()` matches the HAL executable target backend name, but
only recognized the exact string "webgpu". The WebGPU backend registers
its executable target as "webgpu-spirv", so the lookup fell through to
`ClientAPI::Unknown` and WebGPU compilations were stamped with
`api=Unknown` in the `spirv.target_env` attribute.

Accept both "webgpu" and "webgpu-spirv".

The client API is recorded in the spirv.target_env attribute and consumed by upstream MLIR.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[SPIRV] Fix WebGPU SPIR-V client API detection (#25051)

`deduceClientAPI()` matches the HAL executable target backend name, but
only recognized the exact string "webgpu". The WebGPU backend registers
its executable target as "webgpu-spirv", so the lookup fell through to
`ClientAPI::Unknown` and WebGPU compilations were stamped with
`api=Unknown` in the `spirv.target_env` attribute.

Accept both "webgpu" and "webgpu-spirv".

The client API is recorded in the spirv.target_env attribute and consumed by upstream MLIR.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[CMake] Honor IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR for compiler TableGen (#25049)

Honor `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` when locating `iree-tblgen` for compiler builds (`IREE_BUILD_COMPILER=ON`).

`IREE_TABLEGEN_EXE` was set to `$<TARGET_FILE:iree-tblgen>`. With `IREE_ENABLE_THREADING=OFF`, `tools/CMakeLists.txt` hits `return()` before the `iree-tblgen` target is defined, so that reference fails at generate time. The existing `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` import in `tools/CMakeLists.txt` only runs when `IREE_BUILD_COMPILER=OFF`.

In `build_tools/cmake/iree_copts.cmake`, when `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` is set, find `iree-tblgen` with `find_program(... REQUIRED)`. Otherwise keep the existing target-based behavior.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: Analyze (javascript)

`IREE_TABLEGEN_EXE` was set to `$<TARGET_FILE:iree-tblgen>`. With `IREE_ENABLE_THREADING=OFF`, `tools/CMakeLists.txt` hits `return()` before the `iree-tblgen` target is defined, so that reference fails at generate time. The existing `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` import in `tools/CMakeLists.txt` only runs when `IREE_BUILD_COMPILER=OFF`.

In `build_tools/cmake/iree_copts.cmake`, when `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` is set, find `iree-tblgen` with `find_program(... REQUIRED)`. Otherwise keep the existing target-based behavior.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>

Honor `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` when locating `iree-tblgen` for compiler builds (`IREE_BUILD_COMPILER=ON`).

`IREE_TABLEGEN_EXE` was set to `$<TARGET_FILE:iree-tblgen>`. With `IREE_ENABLE_THREADING=OFF`, `tools/CMakeLists.txt` hits `return()` before the `iree-tblgen` target is defined, so that reference fails at generate time. The existing `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` import in `tools/CMakeLists.txt` only runs when `IREE_BUILD_COMPILER=OFF`.

In `build_tools/cmake/iree_copts.cmake`, when `IREE_HOST_BIN_DIR` is set, find `iree-tblgen` with `find_program(... REQUIRED)`. Otherwise keep the existing target-based behavior.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: runtime_tracing :: ubuntu-24.04 :: tracy
